rationale:
The public artifact (#239, 'Fix codeSyntax and BlockParser to respect encodeHtml flag'), the production fix, and the triggering tests all describe one pre-existing defect: inline CodeSyntax.onMatch and FencedCodeBlockSyntax unconditionally called escapeHtml, ignoring the Document.encodeHtml flag. The minimized production patch touches only lib/src/inline_parser.dart and lib/src/block_parser.dart and consists solely of guarding the escapeHtml calls with `parser.document.encodeHtml`; the local rename of `escaped` to `text` is required by the new conditional assignment, so there is no unrelated refactor, feature extension, docs-only, config-only, or test-only content. The trigger does not depend on a new production API: neither `Document(encodeHtml:)`, `parser.document`, `parseInline`, nor `parseLines` appears as an addition in the patch, and the pre-existing test in test/document_test.dart (asserting unescaped '< &' text) shows the encodeHtml flag already existed at the buggy revision, confirming this is a missed-honoring bug rather than a new option. Strict evidence gates all pass on both original and post-minimization runs (build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential with reproduced selectors 'encodeHtml false prevents code block escaping' and its BlockParser variant, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic with 4 fingerprint groups, full_suite.fixed_all_green, matrix.complete runs=50, repetitions>=3), and no failed checks are reported. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this root cause duplicates no active registry entry, and dart-archive/markdown#239 is the supplied allowed key.

Single-defect case: CodeSyntax.onMatch and FencedCodeBlockSyntax unconditionally called escapeHtml, ignoring the pre-existing Document.encodeHtml flag. The minimized production patch (identical to production-fix.patch) changes exactly those two call sites to guard escaping with parser.document.encodeHtml; nothing else. The flag is not introduced by the fix: no change touches document.dart, the fix only reads parser.document.encodeHtml, and test/document_test.dart already contained a pre-existing encodeHtml test ('< &' Text case) at the buggy revision, so the trigger does not depend on a new production API. The trigger patch is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same commit and exercises the reported behavior directly through parseInline and parseLines with encodeHtml false/true. Strict evidence shows both revisions build, the two encodeHtml:false selectors fail in isolation and in the full suite on the buggy revision, the encodeHtml:true selectors pass on both (consistent with default-true behavior being already correct), all four are deterministic across 3 repetitions and green on the fixed revision. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this root cause is not a registry duplicate.
